title: µF, nF, pF: Capacitance Units for Real Circuits
h1: Capacitance units — µF, nF and pF
description: 1 µF = 1000 nF = 10⁶ pF. Bulk decoupling in µF; RF bypass in nF; timing and matching in pF. Off by a decade means broken circuit.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

reviewer.name: Turbo Unit Converter editorial review
reviewer.credential: verified against NIST SP 811 and category-specific ISO references

hero: Same physics, six orders of magnitude in practical values. Datasheets mix units on the same line — read the suffix carefully.
body: Capacitor values span from single picofarads (RF matching) to hundreds of thousands of microfarads (motor start caps). The prefixes are consistent SI, but datasheets and schematics blend them freely.

pF (1–1000 pF): RF matching, crystal load caps, PCB parasitics, timing networks. nF (1–1000 nF): decoupling, filter caps, high-frequency bypass. µF (1–1000 µF): power supply bulk, motor run/start, audio coupling. mF/F: hold-up capacitors, supercapacitors.
Ceramic caps: '104' = 10 × 10⁴ pF = 100 nF = 0.1 µF. '473' = 47 nF. '221' = 220 pF. Old European: '4n7' = 4.7 nF; '2µ2' = 2.2 µF. The letter replaces the decimal point.

Digital IC supply pin needs 100 nF close to the pin (high-frequency bypass) plus 10 µF nearby (mid-frequency reservoir) plus 100 µF at the regulator (bulk). All three cover different frequency decades — designing with a single capacitor value misses two orders of magnitude of impedance.
µF, nF, pF differ by 1000× steps. Marking codes hide behind two-digit + exponent format.

faqs.a: The SI unit — 1 F = 1 C/V. Real capacitors are usually µF and smaller; supercaps hit hundreds of farads.
At GHz frequencies, 1 pF has impedance ~50 Ω — significant for RF.
